questions.question: Describe how a coal-fired power station makes electricity.
questions.expected_answer: Coal is crushed and burnt in a boiler, releasing heat. The heat boils water into high-pressure steam. The steam spins a turbine, and the turbine turns a generator, which changes movement energy into electrical energy.

questions.question: How does electricity get from the power station to your home?
questions.expected_answer: It travels along transmission lines on pylons, part of the national grid. At substations, transformers lower the voltage. It travels along smaller lines or underground cables, through another transformer, then into the home through a meter and the distribution board to the lights and plug points.

questions.question: Why do we say mains electricity travels in a circuit? Name two other ways South Africa makes electricity.
questions.expected_answer: Electricity only flows in a complete circuit, so it flows from the power station to our homes and back, which is why plugs and cables have more than one wire. Other ways: nuclear power at Koeberg, wind farms, solar power stations and hydro power from dams.
